recipes.name: Easy Chicken and Broccoli
ingredients_raw: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into chunks
1 (10 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 cup KRAFT Shredded Three Cheese with a Touch of PHILADELPHIA

steps.text: Grease a large skillet with cooking spray and place over medium-high heat. Cook and stir chicken in the hot skillet until browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add broccoli, condensed soup, and water; stir. Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice. Top with cheese. Cover and cook over low heat for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Chicken and Broccoli
raw_recipe.description: This cheap chicken breast recipe is an easy one-skillet comfort food dish made with frozen broccoli, cream of mushroom soup, cheese, and instant rice.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! Fast and easy. I substituted cream of chicken instead of cream of mushroom and used fresh broccoli. Really great.

I changed this up a bit based on the reviews. I sautéed 1 onion and 3 pressed garlic cloves. Then I added the chicken and added around 1 tsp Italian seasoning, and about an extra half tsp basil leaves, salt and pepper to taste. Then I added one can of half cream of chicken half cream of mushroom and chicken broth vs water. It taste like a really good chicken soup before adding the cheese, but the cheese added to it with a nice and savory flavor, but it could with or without the cheese and be good. Perhaps add a little more chicken broth and leave out the rice add a can of biscuits and bam chicken and dumplings. :D

Season chicken with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Brown chicken with onion and garlic. Deglaze pan with chicken stock, not water. I like fresh steamed broccoli and grated sharp cheddar. French fried onions at the end is a bonus.

I've made this many times. Kids love it. I use almost all same ingredients but arrange them differently. Much better this way as I've tried the other version. First steam diced chicken in broth seasoned with salt and pepper and a little garlic powder until done. Remove and set aside. Add broccoli pieces and diced onion to the broth. Continue cooking in the broth (so much more flavor) until done but not mushy. Drain. Layer chicken into a casserole, alternating w ith sharp cheddar cheese, cream of mushroom soup, and broccoli and onion. No rice! This recipe can stand on its own and is much better without it. Heat in oven until cheese is melted, about 20 minutes.
I have made this twice and it is definitely better when the liquid used is chicken stock. I marinate the chicken beforehand to increase its overall seasoning, too.

Love that this came together on the stovetop. I seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper before cooking since I didn't see any other seasonings in this recipe. I was skeptical about the chicken cooking through in that amount of time, so I added a few minutes and it was perfect. Like some others, I used fresh broccoli so I wanted the extra time for that too. I prefer jasmine rice so I cooked that separately and added near the end when I added the shredded cheese. Definitely will be part of our regular rotation.

This was OK. I used brown rice and cooked it with chicken stock and then stirred it in. This dish would be much better with fresh steamed broccoli, not frozen as called for. Indeed a good meal for busy weeknights.

I made this last night. Very quick and easy weeknight supper! My husband loved it. The only thing I did different was used 1 can of cream of chicken soup and substituted chicken broth for the water. I also steamed the broccoli in the microwave first before adding to other ingredients. I also added some salt and pepper as it was cooking. It was a delicious meal !!

I knew before making this dish it would not have much flavor SOOOO I sauteed onion & garlic before Browning the chicken. used fresh broccoli because it was available at the farmer's market. still rather bland, so I added 2 pkgs of G Washington's Golden. Helped a lot. Still missing flavor and will not make again .

Good basic recipe for a quick weeknight meal. I added chopped onions and garlic when frying the chicken, used fresh broccoli, chicken broth instead of water and threw in a pinch of thyme along with some salt and pepper. Hubby approved.

I added in chopped sweet onion with the chicken and replaced the cups of water with chicken stock/broth (whichever I have handy) and it turned out great! I always also add in extra veggies like cauliflower, carrots and extra broccoli! Our teenage boys love it and so do we!!!
This is so great, you must try it.

I added green onions, celery, and garlic to the chicken while it browns. Also added some paprikaThen with the broccoli I threw in the left over carrots I hadI used frozen cauliflower rice so I had to let it cook a but longer. But it is a pretty dish and very good

A quick meal to throw together on weeknights. I would highly recommend seasoning the chicken with salt and pepper in the very least as it's bland as is. I'm not a huge fan of how mushy this comes out, but I appreciate the easy of just throwing together in one pan. I didn't have frozen broccoli, so I steamed fresh broccoli before throwing it into the pan. Additional seasonings would be a good idea.

Family favorite. Fresh broccoli is always better but I keep frozen on hand. A variety for sauce... I wish a bit of mayo and lemon juice with soup mix and too with durkee fried onions near the end of baking.

I made this but added a few changes. I cooked the chicken in a large frying pan. Added fresh broccoli and cooked for a few minutes to soften the broccoli. I mixed the soup, water and rice in a small sauce pan then combined all ingredients in a baking dish. Sprinkled tillamook 4 cheese on top and baked at 400 for 15 minutes. Amazing!!!!!!
Made it like the recipe. The hubby, that doesn’t like chicken had seconds and said we can use that recipe again!
Loved it! very simple and delicious would suggest using fresh broccoli
This was good. It does need to more seasoning. As other readers have stated it is rather bland.
Very easy and very good
